The purpose of this script is to validate the three datasets used in the Atlantic bluefin tuna project: the DFO Fisheries Atlas, GEBCO 2026 bathymetry and Copernicus GLORYS oceanography. Here, I confirm their suitability by inspecting their layers and variables, CRS, extent, resolution and time coverage. No environmental extraction, statistical analysis or final figure production is performed here.  

# Setup
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

# Load necessary packages
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(tibble)
library(terra)
```

# DFO Fisheries Atlas Validation
The DFO fisheries atlas contains reported commercial landings aggregated into spatial reporting cells between 2019 and 2023. I just need the bluefin tuna layer for this project.

About the dataset: catch weights represent reported commercial landings, not tuna abundance. Fishing effort is unavailable and unreported cells should not be treated as zero catch.

```{r inspect-fisheries-geodatabase}
# Define the location of the original fisheries geodatabase
fisheries_geodatabase_path <- here(
  "data",
  "raw_data",
  "DFO_FisheriesAtlas",
  "Maritimes_Fisheries_Atlas_2019_2023.gdb"
)

# Inspect available spatial layers without importing every layer
fisheries_layer_information <- st_layers(
  fisheries_geodatabase_path
)

# Create a summary of the original geodatabase contents.
fisheries_layer_summary <- tibble(
  layer_name = fisheries_layer_information$name,
  geometry_type = vapply(     
    # vapply converts geometry descriptions to a text column
    fisheries_layer_information$geomtype,
    paste,
    collapse = ", ",
    FUN.VALUE = character(1)
  ),
  feature_count = fisheries_layer_information$features
)

# Display all available layers (not just the shortened tibble output)
print(fisheries_layer_summary, n = Inf)
```

## Bluefin tuna data inspection

```{r inspect-biological-data}

# Identify the layer
bluefin_tuna_layer_name <- "BluefinTuna_Landings_Weight_2019_2023"

# Import
bluefin_tuna_data <- sf::st_read(
  dsn = fisheries_geodatabase_path,
  layer = bluefin_tuna_layer_name,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Inspect attribute names
print(names(bluefin_tuna_data))

# Preview bluefin tuna records
head(bluefin_tuna_data)

```
Attributes 'hexGridID' and 'roundWeight_kg' useful for analysis.
The former is an identifer for each fisheries reporting cell, and the later describes commerical catch weight in kg. 


```{r}
# Define required attributes
required_fisheries_fields <- c(
  "hexGridID",
  "roundWeight_kg"
)
# Identify missing required fields
missing_required_fields <- setdiff(
  required_fisheries_fields,
  names(bluefin_tuna_data)
)

# Extract non-spatial attributes
bluefin_tuna_attributes <- sf::st_drop_geometry(
  bluefin_tuna_data
)

# Summarise required field completeness
fisheries_field_validation <- tibble::tibble(
  dataset = "Atlantic bluefin tuna",
  total_records = nrow(bluefin_tuna_data),

  missing_grid_ids = sum(
    is.na(bluefin_tuna_attributes$hexGridID)
  ),

  missing_catch_weights = sum(
    is.na(bluefin_tuna_attributes$roundWeight_kg)
  ),

  positive_catch_records = sum(
    is.finite(bluefin_tuna_attributes$roundWeight_kg) &
      bluefin_tuna_attributes$roundWeight_kg > 0
  )
)

print(fisheries_field_validation, width = Inf)

# Check if reporting-cell identifiers are duplicated
duplicate_grid_ids <- sum(
  duplicated(bluefin_tuna_attributes$hexGridID) &
    !is.na(bluefin_tuna_attributes$hexGridID)
)
```

The fisheries layers are checked for coorindate systems/geometry validtity and missing values / geograpic extent. 

## Fisheries Spatial Validation

```{r validate-fisheries-data}
bluefin_tuna_geographic <- sf::st_transform(
  bluefin_tuna_data,
  4326 # Transform coordinates to WGS84 for consistent geographic extent calculation (does not change original layer CRS)
    )

    # Calculate geographic extent
bluefin_tuna_extent <- sf::st_bbox(
  bluefin_tuna_geographic
)

# Summarise spatial properties
fisheries_spatial_summary <- tibble(
  dataset = "Atlantic bluefin tuna",

  feature_count = nrow(bluefin_tuna_data),

  crs_epsg = sf::st_crs(bluefin_tuna_data)$epsg,

  geometry_type = paste(
    unique(as.character(
      sf::st_geometry_type(bluefin_tuna_data)
    )),
    collapse = ", "
  ),

  invalid_geometries = sum(
    !sf::st_is_valid(bluefin_tuna_data),
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),

  longitude_min = unname(bluefin_tuna_extent["xmin"]),
  longitude_max = unname(bluefin_tuna_extent["xmax"]),
  latitude_min = unname(bluefin_tuna_extent["ymin"]),
  latitude_max = unname(bluefin_tuna_extent["ymax"])
)

print(fisheries_spatial_summary, width = Inf)

# Inspect attribute names and data types
fisheries_attribute_summary <- tibble(
  attribute_name = names(bluefin_tuna_attributes),

  data_type = vapply(
    bluefin_tuna_attributes,
    function(attribute_values) {
      paste(class(attribute_values), collapse = ", ")
    },
    character(1)
  )
)

print(fisheries_attribute_summary, n = Inf)
```
The environmental datasets were acquired for a study area extending approximately from 68°W to 55°W and 39°N to 48°N given extent of the DFOfisheriesAtlas data to keep downloads manageable.  

```{r define-study-area}
# Record the study area extent for future reference which can be used to aquire targetd enviromental data for the fisheries reporting cells.
study_area_extent <- c(
  longitude_min = -68,
  longitude_max = -55,
  latitude_min = 39,
  latitude_max = 48
)
print(study_area_extent)
```

# GEBCO Bathymetry dataset exploration
GEBCO 2026 bathymetry was downloaded as a GeoTIFF raster for the study area extent. GEBCO provides seabed elevation relative to sea level. Negative values represent locations below sea level. This will be used for mapping. 

```{r}
# Load original raster
gebco_bathymetry <- rast(
  here("data", "raw_data", "GEBCO", "gebco_2026_n48.0_s39.0_w-68.0_e-55.0_geotiff.tif")
)

# Inspect spatial properties
gebco_spatial_summary <- tibble(
  dataset = "GEBCO 2026 Bathymetry",
  coordinate_reference_system = crs(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_min = xmin(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_max = xmax(gebco_bathymetry),
  latitude_min = ymin(gebco_bathymetry),
  latitude_max = ymax(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_resolution = res(gebco_bathymetry)[1],
  latitude_resolution = res(gebco_bathymetry)[2],
  raster_columns = ncol(gebco_bathymetry),
  raster_rows = nrow(gebco_bathymetry),
  missing_cells = global(is.na(gebco_bathymetry), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
)

# Display spatial properties
print(gebco_spatial_summary, width = Inf)

# Inspect elevation values
gebco_elevation_summary <- terra::global(
  gebco_bathymetry,
  fun = c("min", "max", "mean"),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

print(gebco_elevation_summary)
```
The GEBCO raster covers the preliminary study area at 15-arc-second resolution and contains no missing raster cells. It is suitable for deriving bathymetric variables. 

# Copernicus Data Validation

This dataset provides montlhy oceanographic data which can be used to examine sea surface temperature and currents from 2019-2023. For this project, I am only concerned with sea surface temperature. The data is downloaded as a NetCDF file and inspected here. Monthly temperature data from January 2019 to December 2023 will be averaged to create a five-year temperature surface layer that can be mapped.

```{r inspect-copernicus-data}

# Identify the downloaded NetCDF file
copernicus_file_path <- list.files(
  here("data", "raw_data", "Copernicus"),
  pattern = "\\.nc$",
  full.names = TRUE
)


# Inspect available variables
copernicus_variables <- terra::sds(copernicus_file_path)

print(copernicus_variables)
```

## Temperature time coverage

```{r validate-copernicus-time}

# Extract monthly timestamps from the temperature dataset
copernicus_temperature <- copernicus_variables["thetao"]

copernicus_time_summary <- tibble(
  first_observation = min(time(copernicus_temperature)),
  last_observation = max(time(copernicus_temperature)),
  number_of_months = nlyr(copernicus_temperature)
)

print(copernicus_time_summary)

# Confirm it has spatial coverage:
copernicus_spatial_summary <- tibble(
  dataset = "Copernicus GLORYS Temperature",

  coordinate_reference_system = terra::crs(
    copernicus_temperature
  ),

  longitude_min = terra::xmin(copernicus_temperature),
  longitude_max = terra::xmax(copernicus_temperature),

  latitude_min = terra::ymin(copernicus_temperature),
  latitude_max = terra::ymax(copernicus_temperature),

  longitude_resolution = terra::res(copernicus_temperature)[1],
  latitude_resolution = terra::res(copernicus_temperature)[2],

  raster_columns = terra::ncol(copernicus_temperature),
  raster_rows = terra::nrow(copernicus_temperature)
)


print(copernicus_spatial_summary, width = Inf)
```
# Validation Outcome
All datasets were checked and deemed fit for use and comparable for our goal. They have sufficient coverage and spatial extent.
